expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires the agent to actually audit the named user (ci-bot)'s credentials: use ListAccessKeys/GetAccessKeyLastUsed and GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, enumerate what each credential can do in Bedrock with risk tiers, give recommended actions with an AWS doc link, clarify the distinction between 'can do' vs 'did do' (last-used is not proof of Bedrock use, invocation history is in GuardDuty AI Protection/CloudTrail), state the audit is read-only and changed nothing, mask the key to last four chars, never print a full account ID, and end without an offer or follow-up question.

The agent's actual response instead reports that it could not find ci-bot or a matching GuardDuty finding in the account it has access to, and declines to produce the report for the wrong identity. It does not perform the IAM policy audit via GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, does not enumerate Bedrock grants/risk tiers per credential, does not provide an AWS documentation link, and does not include the required disclaimer distinguishing 'can do' from 'did do' via GuardDuty AI Protection/CloudTrail. It does print a full account ID ('account 123456789012'), violating the masking requirement. It also ends with a follow-up question ('To continue, tell me the account ID and region...'), explicitly violating the requirement to end without an offer or follow-up question. It does mention 'read-only' is not explicitly stated (no mention that no changes were made is only implied by "I can't change IAM permissions or access keys myself" - which is close but not matching "audit is read-only and changed nothing"). Key ID is not masked to last four since no key was actually identified for ci-bot (though it does show last four of the key found: 7QXZ and an actual key <key ending in XRN6> is shown in full, not masked).

Overall, the response fails to meet nearly all of the specific substantive requirements of the expected output: no IAM policy audit for the named user, no Bedrock grant/risk enumeration, no documentation link, prints full account ID, shows full access key ID unmasked, and ends with a follow-up question contrary to requirements.</reasoning>
